p1_serialization.was: the revocation happened at COMPLETION, so two restorers both passed the entry checks; one completed, the line was released, a successor was admitted, and the other -- still inside the profile -- reset that successor's checkout and then returned the first one's committed result as its own success
now: THE INTENT TAKES THE EXCLUSION: the writer is revoked in the same transaction that fixes the intent, so a second restorer finds no active writer and never reaches the profile
THE LINE IS LEFT `writing` until completion, so no successor can be admitted across the profile boundary -- grant_writer admits only from idle or correction-ready

IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THE WRITE, the committed completion and the line's active writers are read again: an active writer is exactly what a successor admitted after a release looks like, and is what distinguishes one from this recovery's own crash retry
AFTER THE WRITE, a committed completion is refused as operation-collision rather than replayed -- store.transact would otherwise hand back another call's success as this one's
p1_serialization.crash_retry: a resumed call adopts its own committed intent from the journal, re-proves the exclusion is still HERE, and finishes; it deliberately does not re-take an exclusion it already holds

residual_reported_not_papered_over.what: every check this module can make happens BEFORE restore_checkpoint is called. A second restorer paused INSIDE that call -- past its own guard, before its effect -- is not excluded by any of them, and its effect still resets a successor's checkout.
residual_reported_not_papered_over.measured: test_an_in_flight_duplicate_cannot_reset_a_successors_checkout drives the reviewer's exact interleaving and asserts both halves: the duplicate now REFUSES with operation-collision instead of reporting success, and its effect did run
what_closing_it_would_take: a durable in-flight lease, which needs a schema this Work does not own
or an admission that consults this recovery's completion record, which means changing grant_writer -- and CONTRACT.md freezes ordinary grant behaviour
residual_reported_not_papered_over.not_taken: neither is mine to choose inside this allocation

p1_path_substitution.was: the profile validated the PATHNAME and the checkpoint CONTENTS, so renaming the nominated directory and leaving a symlink with its old name pointed the destructive commands at a tree outside the line; -C follows the link
p1_path_substitution.now: the nominated path must be a real directory rather than a link, its device and inode are pinned by lstat before anything is verified, and they are compared again immediately before each destructive command and once after the last one
p1_path_substitution.why_lstat: a symlink whose target is a directory answers a perfectly good directory to stat; what is pinned is the object the NAME resolves to without following anything
controls: the reviewer's rename-and-symlink substitution, with the outside scratch, tracked bytes and metadata directory all proved untouched
a substitution landing BETWEEN the two writes
a repository that is itself a link, refused outright

p1_historical_owners.was: the reader checked the receipt against a signature recomposed from that same receipt -- internal consistency and nothing about the records it was earned against -- and the act inferred the changes-requested provenance from the committed grant
p1_historical_owners.reader_now: follows writer_for_attempt, checkpoint_of and the committed verdict, comparing identity and immutable relationship only; no mutable predicate, so a later writer and a later checkpoint leave an earlier recovery readable
p1_historical_owners.act_now: reads the committed changes-requested verdict through verdict_of before the intent, so a retained verdict whose principal was edited refuses before any profile write
p1_historical_owners.how_the_verdict_is_reached: one SELECT answers a verdict IDENTITY and verdict_of owns and validates the record. No second column contract for checkpoint_verdicts is created, which is what _verdict_row's own comment is about. Pinned in FINDING.md before editing, as the review required.
